slot.brief: Compare two octahedral complexes of the same metal with a weak-field and a strong-field ligand; state which is paramagnetic with how many unpaired electrons.

stem: Which of the following complexes can exist as cis–trans geometrical isomers?

verdicts.working: [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] is square planar and has cis and trans forms. The others have no cis–trans geometrical isomers.

working:
$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is square planar and has two arrangements: cis and trans.
The other complexes do not have cis–trans geometrical isomers.

Independent check: [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] is square planar and has cis and trans forms. The others have no cis–trans geometrical isomers.
solution: For a square-planar complex of the type $[MA_2B_2]$, identical ligands can be adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans). Thus $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ exists as cis–trans geometrical isomers; the other complexes do not.
